summary: Individual Performance Commitment and Review (IPCRF) Professional Development Plan, strengths, growth areas, and self-reflection.
strengths: Expertise in constructivist 5E inquiry learning design and scientific method coaching.
Strong technical proficiency in educational technology, interactive simulations, and open educational resources.
High rapport and ethical engagement with STE learners and advisory classes.
Proactive participation and contribution to school and division Learning Action Cells (LAC).
growth_areas: Further mastery of advanced inferential statistics for student experimental designs (multivariate analysis).
Expanding peer coaching capacity to support non-specialist science teachers in rural cluster schools.
Publication of action research manuscripts in international refereed Scopus/WoS education journals.

action_plan.objective: Enhance statistical mentorship capabilities for student investigatory projects utilizing R and open statistical packages.
action_plan.intervention: Enroll in DOST/SUC specialized biostatistics workshops and online graduate micro-credentials.
action_plan.resources: Open-source R software, university mentor consultations, DepEd LAC funding

action_plan.objective: Lead a division cluster LAC on contextualized laboratory improvisations for junior high science teachers.
action_plan.intervention: Author a training manual on micro-scale chemistry and low-cost physics demonstrations.
action_plan.resources: CID endorsement, school laboratory facilities, recycled apparatus kits

reflection_notes: Continuous growth as a teacher requires acknowledging that science is an evolving human discipline. By openly learning new computational methods alongside my students, I demonstrate that inquiry does not end when one earns a teaching license; rather, teaching itself is the ultimate lifelong experiment.
